task: Draft a 65–100-word editor's note for a local-history edition of an original fictional shore notebook. Explain the unresolved reading using the supplied diplomatic transcription exactly. The house convention c[?]ve marks one unclear letter; the bracketed question mark is editorial, not punctuation written by the diarist. Do not silently choose a reading or replace the uncertainty with an invented journey. Readers need to know what is unclear and why the map does not resolve it.

facts.text: The project's supplied transcription of Mera Lorn's notebook line is exactly “We reached the c[?]ve at noon.”
Damage obscures the word's second letter; the transcriber cannot distinguish cave from cove.
A map in the same packet marks both a cave and a cove, so it does not settle the reading.
The question mark in brackets was supplied by the transcriber and was not written by Lorn.

forbidden_additions: A definite cave or cove destination
A claim that Lorn inserted a question mark or expressed uncertainty in that mark
An invented route, field visit, alternative manuscript, or newly resolved reading
preserve: We reached the c[?]ve at noon.
Cave and cove remain possible readings
Editorial notation is distinguished from the diarist's own writing
The map contains both features and cannot choose between them
